subject: maleo bird
title: This Bird Buries Its Egg in Volcanic Sand and Never Sees the Chick Fly Away

scenes.text: This chick never meets its parents. It doesn't need to.
The maleo of Sulawesi lays an egg about five times the size of a chicken's.
It buries it deep in black sand heated by the sun or by volcanic ground, then walks away forever.
For two to three months the hot ground does the incubating.
The chick hatches underground, claws up through the sand, and can fly and feed itself within hours.
Fewer than 7,000 breeding pairs are left, and it still flies off on day one, alone.

description:
This chick never meets its parents, and it doesn't need to.
The maleo of Sulawesi, Indonesia, lays an egg about five times the size of a chicken's and buries it deep in beach sand or volcanic soil heated by the sun or geothermal energy. The parents leave and never return. After two to three months of incubation by the hot ground, the chick digs its way to the surface and can fly and find its own food within hours of hatching. Only an estimated 4,000 to 7,000 breeding pairs remain.
What is the toughest start to life in the animal kingdom?
first_comment: Bronx Zoo chicks dug themselves out from under three feet of sand on their first day. Which animal is the most independent newborn you know?
